title: What If You Flew to the Nearest Star at Voyager's Speed?

scenes.text: What if you flew to the nearest star at Voyager's speed? You'd never see it.
Voyager 1 travels about 17 kilometers every second. That's roughly 38,000 miles an hour.
The nearest star, Proxima Centauri, is 4.2 light-years away. That's about 40 trillion kilometers.
At Voyager's speed, the trip takes over 73,000 years. Leave today, and you'd arrive around the year 75,000.
Light covers that same distance in just over four years.
Four years for light. Seventy-three thousand for us. That's why we need faster rockets.
